symptom: Process killed by OOM but free memory available system-wide

diagnostic_steps.action: Read memory.events to confirm cgroup-level OOM (not system-wide)
diagnostic_steps.expected: oom or oom_kill > 0; oom_group_kill if memory.oom.group=1

diagnostic_steps.action: Compare current usage vs configured limit
diagnostic_steps.expected: current near max (or memory.high pressure-throttle exceeded)

diagnostic_steps.action: Find which process inside the cgroup got killed
diagnostic_steps.expected: victim PID + RSS + comm + cgroup path

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify if it's a cgroup-limit issue vs node-pressure
diagnostic_steps.command: # free -h vs the cgroup limit; if free memory >> 0 and only a cgroup is OOMing, it's cgroup-limit not host-pressure
diagnostic_steps.expected: host has free memory; cgroup limit is the bottleneck

fix_steps.action: Raise memory.max if the workload genuinely needs more
fix_steps.command: echo 4G | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/<cg>/memory.max   # OR for systemd: sudo systemctl set-property name.service MemoryMax=4G

fix_steps.action: Set memory.high (soft limit, throttles before OOM) for graceful degradation
fix_steps.validation: workload throttled at 3G but not killed

fix_steps.action: For real leak: profile heap and fix
fix_steps.command: # Java: jcmd <pid> GC.heap_dump /tmp/dump.hprof; eclipse MAT\n# Go: pprof -alloc_space http://localhost:port/debug/pprof/heap\n# C/C++: valgrind --tool=memcheck --leak-check=full
fix_steps.validation: steady-state RSS instead of monotonic growth

symptom: CPU usage low but app slow; cpu.stat shows nr_throttled > 0

diagnostic_steps.expected: nr_throttled > 0 AND throttled_usec growing across samples
e.g. '50000 100000' = 50% of 100ms window — bursty work hits cap then waits

diagnostic_steps.action: Sample CPU usage to see burstiness
diagnostic_steps.expected: average <50% but instantaneous bursts to 100% — confirms bursty

fix_steps.action: Increase quota window (longer period accommodates bursts)
fix_steps.command: echo '500000 1000000' | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/<cg>/cpu.max   # same 50% but 1s window
fix_steps.validation: nr_throttled stops increasing for same load

fix_steps.action: Or, raise the quota outright
For systemd-managed services: use CPUQuota
fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl set-property myapp.service CPUQuota=200%   # 2 CPUs worth
fix_steps.validation: systemd writes a longer window with higher quota

symptom: Setting memory.max in a cgroup has no effect; child cgroups can't be created with memory limits

diagnostic_steps.action: List enabled controllers in the cgroup root
diagnostic_steps.expected: controllers: lists what's available; subtree_control: lists what's enabled FOR CHILDREN

diagnostic_steps.action: Walk up parent cgroups to find where the controller stops being enabled
diagnostic_steps.command: # for d in $(echo <cg-path> | tr / ' '); do echo --- $d; cat .../subtree_control 2>/dev/null; done
diagnostic_steps.expected: identifies the parent that didn't enable the controller

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm cgroup v2 unified hierarchy is active (not v1 / hybrid)
diagnostic_steps.expected: cgroup2 on /sys/fs/cgroup type cgroup2

fix_steps.action: Enable controllers in parent's subtree_control
fix_steps.validation: child cgroups now have memory.max etc.

fix_steps.action: For systemd-managed: set Delegate= so systemd enables controllers in the unit's slice
fix_steps.command: # unit file: [Service]\n# Delegate=memory cpu io pids
fix_steps.validation: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart <unit>; verify controllers in cgroup tree

fix_steps.action: For non-unified hosts (rare in 2024+): convert to v2
fix_steps.command: # Add to grub: systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1; sudo update-grub; reboot

symptom: Cannot move a process into a cgroup that already has child cgroups: EBUSY

diagnostic_steps.expected: presence of subdirs = leaf-only rule violated (cgroup v2 doesn't allow processes in non-leaf nodes)

diagnostic_steps.action: Read the v2 'no internal processes' rule
diagnostic_steps.command: # cgroup v2: a non-root cgroup can either contain processes OR have children, not both — once a controller is enabled in subtree_control, the cgroup becomes 'domain' and can't hold procs
diagnostic_steps.expected: yes

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if you're trying to move process to a domain cgroup
diagnostic_steps.expected: 'domain' = can't hold procs once children exist

fix_steps.action: Move process into a leaf cgroup (create one if needed)
fix_steps.validation: echo succeeds; process appears in leaf/cgroup.procs

fix_steps.action: For systemd-managed workloads: use sub-units / scopes
fix_steps.validation: systemd creates a leaf scope automatically

fix_steps.action: Avoid the issue altogether — write process into target BEFORE enabling controllers in the parent
fix_steps.command: # proc-then-controllers ordering means the cgroup is still type=domain-threaded; works

symptom: Bursty workload throttled even though long-run CPU usage well under quota

diagnostic_steps.expected: nr_throttled > 0; throttled_usec > 0; quota in 100ms window
avg ~30% but spikes to 200-400% (bursts)

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if cgroup v2 burst feature is available
diagnostic_steps.expected: cpu.max.burst exists on kernel >= 5.14

fix_steps.action: Increase quota period (longer window absorbs bursts)
fix_steps.command: echo '500000 1000000' | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/<cg>/cpu.max   # 50% of 1s instead of 50% of 100ms

fix_steps.action: Or, on kernel >= 5.14, allow CPU burst beyond quota
fix_steps.command: echo 50000 | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/<cg>/cpu.max.burst   # accumulate up to 50ms of unused quota

fix_steps.action: For systemd: CPUQuotaPeriodSec= (longer period)

symptom: Process has cap in PERMITTED but not EFFECTIVE; operation fails EPERM

diagnostic_steps.expected: CapInh, CapPrm, CapEff, CapBnd, CapAmb shown as hex bitmaps

diagnostic_steps.action: Decode the bitmaps to capability names
diagnostic_steps.expected: human-readable list; check if expected cap is missing
file caps determine what the new exec'd process can have

fix_steps.action: Set ambient cap on the launcher process tree
fix_steps.command: # in launcher: prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT, PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE, CAP_X)\n# OR run via 'capsh --caps=cap_x+pi --addamb=cap_x -- -c "./mybin"'
fix_steps.validation: CapAmb shows the cap; child inherits in CapEff

fix_steps.action: Or set file capability (binary gets cap on every exec)
fix_steps.validation: getcap shows cap_x+eip; exec'd process has cap

fix_steps.action: For systemd-managed services: AmbientCapabilities
fix_steps.validation: systemd applies; service can bind low ports

symptom: Outbound clients fail EADDRNOTAVAIL after burst of short-lived connections

diagnostic_steps.expected: >> 28k = ephemeral pool likely exhausted
e.g. '32768 60999' = ~28k usable; if low, less headroom
tw_reuse=0 (default) → can't reuse TIME-WAIT for new outbound; max_tw_buckets cap

fix_steps.action: Widen ephemeral port range
Enable tw_reuse for outbound (clients only — safe RFC 6191)
fix_steps.validation: outbound bind succeeds even with TIME-WAITs

fix_steps.action: Use connection pooling in the app (root-cause fix)
fix_steps.command: # keep persistent HTTP/2 / gRPC connections; HTTP keep-alive; reuse DB connections via pool
fix_steps.validation: new TIME-WAITs growth slows; usually drops by 90%+

symptom: `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` in dmesg; new connections silently fail

diagnostic_steps.expected: count near max (>80% = approaching exhaustion)

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm dmesg has the table-full warning
diagnostic_steps.expected: 'table full, dropping packet' message at incident time

diagnostic_steps.command: sudo conntrack -L | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
diagnostic_steps.expected: often dominated by TCP TIME_WAIT entries that haven't expired

fix_steps.action: Raise table size
fix_steps.command: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1048576   # also raise hashsize: echo 262144 | sudo tee /sys/module/nf_conntrack/parameters/hashsize

fix_steps.action: Lower TIME_WAIT/UDP timeouts so flows expire faster
Add NOTRACK rule for high-volume internal traffic that doesn't need state
fix_steps.command: sudo nft add rule ip raw prerouting ip saddr 10.0.0.0/8 notrack

symptom: DNS queries slow inside container; first lookup takes multi-second

diagnostic_steps.expected: high ndots (e.g. ndots:5) + many search domains

diagnostic_steps.action: Time a no-trailing-dot lookup vs FQDN
diagnostic_steps.command: time getent hosts api.github.com 2>&1; time getent hosts api.github.com. 2>&1
diagnostic_steps.expected: trailing-dot fast (<100ms); no-trailing slow (multi-second) = search amplification

diagnostic_steps.action: Cross-check with a direct dig to the resolver
diagnostic_steps.expected: <100ms = upstream is fast; slow lookup is search-side, not upstream

fix_steps.action: Lower ndots in resolv.conf
fix_steps.command: # Append: options ndots:1   # OR ndots:2 if cluster-internal short names matter\necho 'options ndots:1' | sudo tee -a /etc/resolv.conf

fix_steps.action: Use FQDN with trailing dot in app code
For containers in k8s: use spec.dnsConfig.options ndots:2
fix_steps.validation: new pods see ndots:2 in resolv.conf

symptom: After IP move (failover, container restart), host can't reach VIP for 5-30s; arp -an shows wrong MAC

diagnostic_steps.expected: INCOMPLETE/STALE/FAILED entry for VIP, OR an entry pointing at the OLD MAC

diagnostic_steps.action: Compare to actual MAC of the IP holder
diagnostic_steps.expected: arping reply MAC vs ip neigh entry — if different, cache is stale

diagnostic_steps.action: Check whether sysctls are tuned for fast invalidation
diagnostic_steps.expected: defaults can leave stale entries for tens of seconds

fix_steps.action: From the new IP owner: send gratuitous ARP
On peers: invalidate cache for that IP
fix_steps.command: sudo ip neigh flush <vip>   # OR: sudo ip neigh del <vip> dev eth0
fix_steps.validation: new ARP request sent on next packet

fix_steps.action: Tune sysctls for faster invalidation in HA setups

symptom: Idle TCP connections through NAT are silently dropped after ~5 minutes

diagnostic_steps.expected: 7200/75/9 = first probe after 2 hours (way past most NAT timers)

diagnostic_steps.command: # typical: AWS NLB 350s, AWS ALB 60s default, stateful firewall 300s
diagnostic_steps.expected: <7200s — NAT will drop the connection before kernel keepalive fires

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm app even has SO_KEEPALIVE enabled
diagnostic_steps.expected: keepalive timer present per socket — if absent, kernel never probes

fix_steps.action: Lower app keepalive (per-socket via SO_KEEPALIVE+TCP_KEEPIDLE)
Or system-wide, lower tcp_keepalive_time
fix_steps.validation: defaults more aggressive; affects all sockets with SO_KEEPALIVE

fix_steps.action: App-side: send periodic application-level pings
fix_steps.command: # HTTP/2 PING frames; gRPC keepalive: 30s; WebSocket ping/pong
fix_steps.validation: connection stays warm via app traffic, NAT timer never fires

symptom: App using EPOLLET stops getting events for some FDs even though data arrived

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if app is using EPOLLET (edge-triggered)
diagnostic_steps.expected: yes

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify app drains FD until EAGAIN
diagnostic_steps.command: # strace or code review of read() loop on each EPOLLIN — does it loop until EAGAIN?
diagnostic_steps.expected: if app does single read() per event, it'll miss subsequent data
required for EPOLLET to work correctly

fix_steps.action: On EPOLLET, loop read() until EAGAIN before going back to epoll_wait
fix_steps.command: # while ((n = read(fd, buf, sizeof buf)) > 0) handle_data(buf, n);\n# if (n < 0 && errno != EAGAIN) handle_error();
fix_steps.validation: all FDs serviced; no missed events

fix_steps.action: Make all FDs non-blocking
fix_steps.command: # int flags = fcntl(fd, F_GETFL, 0); fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK);
fix_steps.validation: read returns EAGAIN instead of blocking

fix_steps.action: Or switch to level-triggered (EPOLLET removed) if read-loop pattern is hard to retrofit
fix_steps.validation: events repeat until drained; safer default

symptom: Server gets wrong UID via SCM_CREDENTIALS on AF_UNIX

diagnostic_steps.action: Check setsockopt SO_PASSCRED was enabled on the receiving socket
diagnostic_steps.command: # code review or strace: setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PASSCRED, &one, sizeof one)
diagnostic_steps.expected: if missing, no SCM_CREDENTIALS arrives

diagnostic_steps.action: Check what's in the ucred when received
diagnostic_steps.expected: compare to expected client uid
AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM

fix_steps.action: Enable SO_PASSCRED on receiver before recvmsg
fix_steps.command: # server: int one=1; setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PASSCRED, &one, sizeof one);
fix_steps.validation: SCM_CREDENTIALS arrives in cmsg with correct uid

fix_steps.action: For peer credentials at connect time (not per-message)
For abstract-namespace sockets, prefer SO_PEERCRED (avoids cmsg complexity)
fix_steps.command: # socket bound to '\0name' instead of /var/run/foo.sock; same SO_PEERCRED works

symptom: `mount --bind -o ro` doesn't actually mark target readonly

diagnostic_steps.expected: shows 'rw' despite -o ro on the bind — known bind-mount quirk
succeeds despite intent for readonly

diagnostic_steps.command: # bind mounts inherit source's mount flags; -o ro is silently ignored on initial bind
diagnostic_steps.expected: yes

fix_steps.action: Two-step: bind, then remount RO
For systemd mount units
fix_steps.command:
# [Mount]
# What=/src
# Where=/dst
# Options=bind,ro
# Type=none
# (newer systemd handles the two-step internally)

fix_steps.action: For ephemeral containers/scripts: use a fresh mount namespace

symptom: Mount slow after crash; dmesg shows 'orphan inode list' replay

diagnostic_steps.expected: orphan inode replay messages near boot/mount time
Filesystem state: clean (or 'clean with errors')
Journal size, last journal write timestamp

fix_steps.action: Allow fsck to clean orphans
fix_steps.command: sudo umount <mount> && sudo e2fsck -y -f <dev> && sudo mount <mount>

fix_steps.action: For root fs: schedule fsck on next boot
fix_steps.command: sudo touch /forcefsck   # OR: sudo tune2fs -i 1 <dev>   # force interval check

fix_steps.action: Increase journal size if recovery is consistently slow
fix_steps.command: # offline: sudo tune2fs -O ^has_journal <dev>; sudo tune2fs -J size=256 <dev>
fix_steps.validation: larger journal absorbs more pending writes

symptom: `/tmp` write fails ENOSPC; size shows 50% but tmpfs default is 50% of RAM

diagnostic_steps.expected: size= option in mount line; df shows usage near limit
identifies large files

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if memory pressure caused tmpfs eviction
diagnostic_steps.command: # tmpfs is RAM-backed; high mem pressure can cause swapping or OOM
diagnostic_steps.expected: free -h shows low free + tmpfs counts as MemUsed

fix_steps.action: Resize tmpfs without unmount
Persist via fstab
Or move heavy workload off /tmp to disk-backed dir
fix_steps.validation: app uses disk instead of RAM-tmpfs

symptom: `setfattr` fails 'Operation not supported'

diagnostic_steps.action: Check fs supports xattr at all
diagnostic_steps.command: sudo tune2fs -l <dev> 2>/dev/null | grep -i features   # for ext
diagnostic_steps.expected: 'user_xattr' feature flag should be set; if missing, fs doesn't support xattrs
if 'nouser_xattr' in options, xattrs blocked

diagnostic_steps.action: Test on a different fs (rule out target binary issue)
diagnostic_steps.expected: works on tmpfs/ext4 if binary is fine

fix_steps.action: Mount with user_xattr
For ext fs without the feature at create time, enable via tune2fs
fix_steps.command: sudo tune2fs -O user_xattr <dev>   # may need fs to be unmounted

fix_steps.action: Persist mount option in fstab

symptom: App with FAN_CLASS_CONTENT seems hung; access to watched files freezes

diagnostic_steps.command: # fanotify-aware processes are in 'D' / 'S' state; check /proc/*/fd for fanotify fd
diagnostic_steps.expected: finds the listener

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify the listener is actually reading + responding
diagnostic_steps.expected: reads fanotify_event_metadata; writes fanotify_response — if just reading, never replying

diagnostic_steps.command: # default: kernel waits forever for FAN_ALLOW/FAN_DENY response
diagnostic_steps.expected: yes — explains the hang

fix_steps.action: Always reply with FAN_RESPONSE within reasonable time
fix_steps.command: # struct fanotify_response resp = { .fd = ev->fd, .response = FAN_ALLOW };\n# write(fan_fd, &resp, sizeof(resp));

fix_steps.action: For broken/crashed listener: kill it (kernel falls back to allow)
fix_steps.command: # pkill <listener>; or close its fanotify fd

fix_steps.action: Use FAN_NOTIF (notification-only) instead of FAN_CLASS_CONTENT for monitoring without blocking
fix_steps.validation: events delivered but no permission gating

symptom: Flame graph shows shallow stacks; symbols mostly '[unknown]'

diagnostic_steps.action: Check perf was given a call-graph option
diagnostic_steps.command: # what perf record command did you use?
diagnostic_steps.expected: perf record without -g/--call-graph = no stacks at all

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if the binary has frame pointers
diagnostic_steps.command: # objdump -d /path/to/bin | head -20  — look for push %rbp / mov %rsp,%rbp prologue
diagnostic_steps.expected: if missing, fp unwind fails → use dwarf

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify perf has access to debug symbols
diagnostic_steps.expected: if [unknown] dominates, install debug-symbols package

fix_steps.action: Use DWARF unwinding (works without frame pointers)
For better fidelity, recompile target with frame pointers
fix_steps.command: # add CFLAGS+=' -fno-omit-frame-pointer' (cheaper than dwarf at runtime)

fix_steps.action: Install debug symbols for libraries
fix_steps.command: sudo apt install -y libc6-dbg <pkg>-dbg   # or -dbgsym packages
fix_steps.validation: flame graph shows symbol names instead of [unknown]

symptom: `bpftrace` or `bcc` script fails: 'verifier failed' on attach

diagnostic_steps.command: # bpftrace -v ./script.bt   # OR: BCC_LOGLEVEL=DEBUG ./tool   # OR: bpftool prog load <obj> /sys/fs/bpf/x type ... and read syslog
diagnostic_steps.expected: verifier log points at the offending instruction

diagnostic_steps.action: Check kernel version (verifier improves with each release)
diagnostic_steps.expected: if old kernel (<5.4), verifier may reject programs that work on newer

diagnostic_steps.command: # default 1M instruction limit; or stack-depth limit
diagnostic_steps.expected: long unrolled loops or deep stacks may exceed

fix_steps.action: Bound the program: hard-code loop limit, narrow types
fix_steps.command: # replace 'for ($i=0; ...)' with bpf_for + small N\n# replace u64 with u32 where possible (smaller register state)

fix_steps.action: Use BTF-aware kfunc when available (better type checking, easier verifier)
Use bounded helpers instead of arbitrary memory access
fix_steps.command: # bpf_probe_read_kernel/_user with explicit size (not arbitrary deref)

symptom: App becomes 100x slower under `strace -f`; production user-impacting

diagnostic_steps.command: # benchmark with vs without strace -f attached
diagnostic_steps.expected: big perf delta (10-100x for syscall-heavy apps)
hot syscalls = the multiplier

diagnostic_steps.action: Check whether the app's slowness is genuinely syscall-heavy (the only case strace really hurts)
diagnostic_steps.expected: high syscall rate confirms ptrace is the bottleneck

fix_steps.action: Use strace -e trace=<subset> to limit which syscalls are traced
Switch to bpftrace tracepoints (lower overhead)
Or perf trace (very low overhead alternative to strace)

symptom: `systemctl set-property MemoryMax=2G` does nothing visible; cgroup memory.max unchanged

diagnostic_steps.expected: shows new value if accepted; if 'infinity', wasn't applied
=yes (without it, the limit is set but not enforced)
matches the value you set; if 'max', didn't take

fix_steps.action: Use --runtime=false to persist + reload
fix_steps.command: sudo systemctl set-property myapp.service MemoryMax=2G && sudo systemctl daemon-reload

fix_steps.action: Enable accounting (required for some properties to take effect)
For cgroup v1 hosts: enable in /etc/systemd/system.conf

symptom: Long-running systemd service killed before finishing graceful shutdown

diagnostic_steps.expected: see TimeoutStopSec exceeded; SIGKILL message
default 90s; if your shutdown takes longer, this is the issue

diagnostic_steps.command: # log inspection: does the app log 'received SIGTERM, shutting down'?
diagnostic_steps.expected: if no log, app is silently dropping signal

fix_steps.action: Raise TimeoutStopSec
fix_steps.command: # unit file: [Service]\n# TimeoutStopSec=300s\nsudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart myapp
fix_steps.validation: graceful exit completes within new window

fix_steps.action: Use SIGTERM-aware code in app
fix_steps.command: # trap SIGTERM, drain in-flight work, exit cleanly

fix_steps.action: For services that need notify-on-shutdown: KillSignal + SendSIGKILL
fix_steps.command:
# [Service]
# KillSignal=SIGTERM
# KillMode=mixed
# SendSIGKILL=no   # OR yes with longer TimeoutStopSec

symptom: User code can't write to its own cgroup tree even though it owns the slice

diagnostic_steps.expected: =yes for full control; if =no, systemd manages all cgroup files
list of controllers (cpu, memory, io, pids)

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify by attempting to write subtree_control
diagnostic_steps.expected: if EACCES, delegation isn't set

fix_steps.action: Set Delegate=yes (and which controllers)
fix_steps.command: # unit: [Service]\n# Delegate=cpu memory io pids\nsudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart myapp

fix_steps.action: For container runtimes (docker/runc/containerd): typically need full delegation
For user services (systemd --user), enable Delegate at the user-manager level

symptom: Container PID 1 not reaping; zombies pile up

diagnostic_steps.command: docker exec <c> sh -c 'ps axo pid,ppid,stat,comm | grep -E "Z|<defunct>"'
diagnostic_steps.expected: non-zero count; check growth over time

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify what's PID 1 in the container
diagnostic_steps.expected: if your app or 'sh', it's not designed to reap orphan zombies

diagnostic_steps.action: Find the reaper-needed parent (PPID of zombies)
diagnostic_steps.command: docker exec <c> ps axo pid,ppid,stat,comm | awk '$3 ~ /^Z/ {print $2}' | sort -u
diagnostic_steps.expected: PPID = 1 → PID 1 isn't reaping; PPID = N → that process isn't reaping

fix_steps.action: Run with --init (docker injects tini as PID 1)
fix_steps.validation: PID 1 = docker-init; zombies disappear, new ones don't accumulate

fix_steps.action: For app PID 1 that forks: install SIGCHLD handler
fix_steps.command: # C: signal(SIGCHLD, handler) where handler does waitpid(-1, &st, WNOHANG) in loop\n# Python: signal.signal(signal.SIGCHLD, ...)

fix_steps.action: For Compose: init: true at the service level
fix_steps.validation: compose creates containers with docker-init as PID 1
